review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

7:1.sourceText: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἶδον τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὰς τέσσαρας γωνίας τῆς γῆς, κρατοῦντας τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀνέμους τῆς γῆς, ἵνα μὴ πνέῃ ἄνεμος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μήτε ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης μήτε ἐπὶ πᾶν δένδρον.
7:1.targetText: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back its four winds so that no wind would blow on land or sea or on any tree.

groups.note: τῆς γῆς ("of the earth") is rendered its.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not repeat on before sea.

7:2.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἀναβαίνοντα ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου, ἔχοντα σφραγῖδα Θεοῦ ζῶντος, καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τοῖς τέσσαρσιν ἀγγέλοις οἷς ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἀδικῆσαι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν,
7:2.targetText: And I saw another angel ascending from the east, with the seal of the living God. And he called out in a loud voice to the four angels who had been given power to harm the land and the sea:

groups.note: ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου ("the rising of the sun") together mean the east.
The participle ἔχοντα ("having") is rendered with.
The dative φωνῇ supplies in.
The dative ἀγγέλοις supplies to.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive αὐτοῖς repeats οἷς ("to whom") and has no separate English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the thing given; ἐδόθη ("it was given") has no noun.

7:3.sourceText: λέγων Μὴ ἀδικήσητε τὴν γῆν μήτε τὴν θάλασσαν μήτε τὰ δένδρα, ἄχρι σφραγίσωμεν τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
7:3.targetText: “Do not harm the land or sea or trees until we have sealed the foreheads of the servants of our God.”

groups.note: BSB names the servants as the owners of the foreheads, so the genitive αὐτῶν ("their") is rendered of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB introduces the speech with a colon at the end of 7:2, leaving λέγων ("saying") without an English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB makes the foreheads the object of sealed, so ἐπί ("on") has no English word.

7:4.sourceText: Καὶ ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἐσφραγισμένων, ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ·
7:4.targetText: And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel:

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐσφραγισμένων ("of the ones sealed") is rendered of those who were sealed.
ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες ("a hundred forty-four thousands") together mean 144,000.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat sealed after the number.
BSB renders "the tribe of the sons of Israel" as the tribes of Israel, leaving υἱῶν ("sons") without an English word.

7:5.sourceText: ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι, ἐκ φυλῆς Ῥουβὴν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Γὰδ δώδεκα χιλιάδες,
7:5.targetText: From the tribe of Judah 12,000 were sealed, from the tribe of Reuben 12,000, from the tribe of Gad 12,000,

groups.note: δώδεκα χιλιάδες ("twelve thousands") together mean 12,000.
The perfect passive participle ἐσφραγισμένοι ("sealed") is rendered as a finite verb.

7:6.sourceText: ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσὴρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Νεφθαλεὶμ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Μανασσῆ δώδεκα χιλιάδες,
7:6.targetText: from the tribe of Asher 12,000, from the tribe of Naphtali 12,000, from the tribe of Manasseh 12,000,

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

7:7.sourceText: ἐκ φυλῆς Συμεὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Λευεὶ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰσσαχὰρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες,
7:7.targetText: from the tribe of Simeon 12,000, from the tribe of Levi 12,000, from the tribe of Issachar 12,000,

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

7:8.sourceText: ἐκ φυλῆς Ζαβουλὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰωσὴφ δώδεκα χιλιάδες, ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμεὶν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι.
7:8.targetText: from the tribe of Zebulun 12,000, from the tribe of Joseph 12,000, and from the tribe of Benjamin 12,000.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat sealed at the end of the list (see 7:5).

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds and before the last tribe of the list; the Greek has no καί.

7:9.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ ὄχλος πολύς, ὃν ἀριθμῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο, ἐκ παντὸς ἔθνους καὶ φυλῶν καὶ λαῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν, ἑστῶτες ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Ἀρνίου, περιβεβλημένους στολὰς λευκάς, καὶ φοίνικες ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῶν·
7:9.targetText: After this I looked and saw a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.

groups.note: The plural ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered this.
ἰδού ("behold") is rendered saw.
BSB turns "which no one could count" into too large to count, so too carries οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ("no one could").
The participle περιβεβλημένους ("clothed in") is rendered as a finite verb.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's to count has no object, so the relative ὅν and the resumptive αὐτόν ("which … it") have no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle.
English supplies a verb; the Greek has only palm branches in their hands.

7:10.sourceText: καὶ κράζουσιν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες Ἡ σωτηρία τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ Ἀρνίῳ.
7:10.targetText: And they cried out in a loud voice:  “Salvation to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”

groups.note: The present κράζουσιν is rendered with an English past.
The dative φωνῇ supplies in.
The dative Θεῷ supplies to.
The article with the participle καθημένῳ ("the one sitting") is rendered who sits.
The dative Ἀρνίῳ supplies to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB introduces the speech with a colon, leaving λέγοντες ("saying") without an English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:11.sourceText: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι εἱστήκεισαν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων, καὶ ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ,
7:11.targetText: And all the angels stood around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures. And they fell facedown before the throne and worshiped God,

groups.note: The one κύκλῳ covers all three groups; BSB repeats around before the elders.
ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ("on their faces") is rendered facedown.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:12.sourceText: λέγοντες Ἀμήν, ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ σοφία καὶ ἡ εὐχαριστία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ ἰσχὺς τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
7:12.targetText: saying, “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanks and honor and power and strength be to our God forever and ever! Amen.”

groups.note: The dative Θεῷ supplies to.
The genitive τῶν αἰώνων ("of the ages") completes the idiom forever and ever; there is no separate Greek and.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

7:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγων μοι Οὗτοι οἱ περιβεβλημένοι τὰς στολὰς τὰς λευκὰς τίνες εἰσὶν καὶ πόθεν ἦλθον;
7:13.targetText: Then one of the elders addressed me: “These in white robes,” he asked, “who are they, and where have they come from?”

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη ("answered") is rendered addressed.
The participle λέγων ("saying") is rendered as a finite verb.
The article with the participle περιβεβλημένοι ("the ones clothed in") is rendered in.
πόθεν means "from where".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle λέγων.

7:14.sourceText: καὶ εἴρηκα αὐτῷ Κύριέ μου, σὺ οἶδας. καὶ εἶπέν μοι Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι ἐκ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἔπλυναν τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐλεύκαναν αὐτὰς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Ἀρνίου.
7:14.targetText: “Sir,” I answered, “you know.”  So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

groups.note: The perfect εἴρηκα ("I have said") is rendered I answered.
Κύριέ μου ("my lord") is a polite address, rendered Sir.
The article with the participle ἐρχόμενοι ("the ones coming") is rendered the ones who have come.
ἐλεύκαναν ("they whitened") is rendered made … white.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the reply without and, so καί has no English word.
BSB leaves the indirect objects αὐτῷ ("to him") and μοι ("to me") without an English word.
The repeated article of the adjective μεγάλης has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new clause after a semicolon and leaves καί unrendered.

7:15.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτό εἰσιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ λατρεύουσιν αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου σκηνώσει ἐπ’ αὐτούς.
7:15.targetText: For this reason,  they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered For this reason.
The article with the participle καθήμενος ("the one sitting") is rendered the One seated.
σκηνώσει ("will tabernacle, will dwell as in a tent") is rendered will spread … tabernacle.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a possessive; the Greek verb has no object.

7:16.sourceText: οὐ πεινάσουσιν ἔτι οὐδὲ διψήσουσιν ἔτι, οὐδὲ μὴ πέσῃ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὁ ἥλιος οὐδὲ πᾶν καῦμα,
7:16.targetText: ‘Never again will they hunger, and never will they thirst; nor will the sun beat down upon them, nor any scorching heat.’

groups.note: οὐδὲ … ἔτι ("nor … any longer") is rendered and never.
οὐδὲ μή is an emphatic negative, rendered nor.
The subjunctive πέσῃ ("fall") is rendered as an English future under οὐδὲ μή.

7:17.sourceText: ὅτι τὸ Ἀρνίον τὸ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ θρόνου ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς καὶ ὁδηγήσει αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ ζωῆς πηγὰς ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐξαλείψει ὁ Θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
7:17.targetText: For the Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd. ‘He will lead them to springs of living water,’ and ‘God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.’”

groups.note: ποιμανεῖ ("will shepherd") is rendered will be … shepherd.
The object αὐτούς ("them") is rendered their with shepherd.
The genitive ζωῆς ("of life") is rendered living.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article of the phrase ἀνὰ μέσον has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
